verdict: PepsiCo grew revenue 5.6% to $25.3B as its international businesses did the heavy lifting — every international segment grew — while North America foods stayed flat, and operating profit jumped 19% helped by one-time acquisition and divestiture credits.

segments.name: PepsiCo Foods North America
segments.note: Frito-Lay snacks and Quaker foods in North America — flat versus a year ago, though savory-snack volumes and market share improved.

segments.name: PepsiCo Beverages North America
segments.note: Drinks in North America — growth came mainly from acquisitions made in 2025.

segments.name: International Beverages Franchise
segments.note: Concentrate and franchise fees from bottlers outside North America.

segments.name: Europe, Middle East & Africa
segments.note: Foods and drinks across EMEA — the largest international segment.

segments.name: Latin America Foods
segments.note: Snacks and foods in Latin America — the fastest-growing segment, with volume growth.

segments.name: Asia Pacific Foods
segments.note: Foods in Asia Pacific — double-digit growth on organic volume.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling, advertising, distribution support and the back office.

otherDetail: Other pension and retiree medical benefits cost $114M and net interest expense and other cost $242M; $22M of the remaining profit belonged to noncontrolling interests.
follow100Note: For every $100 of sales, $12.06 was kept as profit for PepsiCo shareholders. Rows are rounded to cents.

takeaways.title: International did the growing
takeaways.text: Every international segment grew — Latin America Foods +14%, Asia Pacific +10%, EMEA and the franchise drinks business +8% each. International brought in $11.1B of the $25.3B total.

takeaways.title: North America foods is stuck
takeaways.text: PepsiCo Foods North America was flat at $6.5B and its operating profit fell 13%. Management said it is acting 'with urgency' to improve North America with more innovation and sharper execution.

takeaways.title: Core profit grew much slower than the headline
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS rose 17% to $2.23, but core EPS — PepsiCo's cleaned-up measure — rose only 2% to $2.34, and core operating profit rose 3% while its margin shrank. The gap is one-time items, listed below.

oneTimers: GAAP operating profit was lifted by one-time items: a $96M net credit from acquisition and divestiture items and mark-to-market gains on commodity derivatives, partly offset by $192M of restructuring and impairment charges. Stripping them out, core operating profit was $4,277M, up 3%.
Last year's quarter carried a $133M impairment of the Rockstar brand ($2.0B year-to-date), which flatters this year's 19% operating-profit growth comparison.
footerNote: PepsiCo's fiscal third quarter covers the 12 weeks ended September 5, 2026.
